themes.name: Hand-only 3D pose and mesh from RGB images or short clips (object treated as an occluder)
themes.what_papers_do: A network takes a hand crop (single image, short clip, or several calibrated or uncalibrated views) and outputs MANO parameters or 3D joints for one or two hands. The object is not estimated; it only appears as occlusion. Method mix: large ViT regressors trained on scaled pseudo-labelled data (HaMeR, WiLoR lineage) are about half the rows. The rest are Mamba backbones (Hamba, DF-Mamba), discrete-token or VQ-MANO masked modelling (TokenHand, MaskHand), diffusion priors (HHMR, affordance-guided prior, cascaded diffusion), contrastive pre-training (SiMHand, HandCLR), geometry-foundation features (GeoHand with MoGe-2, HGGT with VGGT), and about 5 temporal-clip models (low-resolution video, prior-aware temporal modelling, UniHand, ConTrack, a generative temporal transformer).

themes.name: Single-frame joint estimation of hand pose and held-object pose or shape
themes.what_papers_do: From one RGB frame (occasionally one RGB-D frame, a stereo pair or sparse views), these papers jointly estimate the MANO hand and either the 6-DoF pose of a known object or the shape of an unknown held object. Shape is represented as an SDF, occupancy, point cloud, NeRF, Gaussians or a generated mesh. Method mix: about half are hand-conditioned implicit or transformer decoders (HOISDF, HORT, MCC-HO, UniHOPE, HOPformer, QORT-Former). A diffusion group (D-SCo point-cloud diffusion, Follow My Hold latent diffusion) is another strand. A rising foundation-model group initializes the object with image-to-3D or text-to-3D models and then refines the interaction by optimization (EasyHOI, TIGeR, GraspHOI). Contact-field and masked-pretraining rows round out the set.

themes.name: Template-free hand-object reconstruction from monocular video (per-sequence optimization, Gaussian splatting, foundation-model priors)
themes.what_papers_do: Given a monocular RGB video of one or two hands manipulating an unknown rigid or articulated object, these papers recover the hand trajectory, the object shape and the per-frame object 6-DoF pose (or articulation) up to scale. Method mix: about 9 rows run per-sequence optimization of neural SDFs or meshes (HOLD, IHoR, the CVPR 2025 dynamic-interaction method, TexHOI). About 9 use 3D or 4D Gaussian splatting (BIGS, GHOST, Clay-to-Stone, Interaction-aware 4DGS, Grasp in Gaussians, the HANDS challenge entries). The rest use generative priors (G-HOP diffusion prior, MagicHOI novel-view diffusion, AGILE VLM-guided generation, CHOIR) or a feed-forward predictor (ForeHOI). Initialization comes from HaMeR/WiLoR, SAM/SAM3D and image-to-3D models.

themes.name: World-grounded hand and hand-object motion from moving (mostly egocentric) cameras
themes.what_papers_do: These papers lift camera-space hand estimates into a consistent world frame for a moving or head-mounted camera. They decouple hand motion from a camera trajectory obtained by SLAM or by feed-forward geometry models (CUT3R, MoGe). Motion-diffusion priors infill hands that leave the view and remove jitter. Recent rows add the 6-DoF object (WHOLE, EgoGrasp) or the full body and scene (EgoAllo, REWIND, ReViV, Hand3R).

themes.name: Physics-aware refinement and tracking of hand and hand-object motion
themes.what_papers_do: These papers take noisy hand or hand-object trajectories from vision trackers, or perceive with physics in the loop, and make the result physically plausible. They remove penetration, floating contact and sliding, and enforce biomechanical limits. Method mix: learned diffusion denoisers make up about half (GeneOH, Physics-Aware HOI Denoising, intuitive-physics diffusion, PAD-Hand with Euler-Lagrange residuals). The rest are an RL controller in MuJoCo (HOIC), simulator-in-the-loop CMA-ES (Grasp-and-Lift), coupled inverse dynamics (DynamicHOI), differentiable physics and rendering priors (HandyPriors), and a musculoskeletal MANO extension (MS-MANO).

themes.name: Hand (and occluded-object) estimation from depth, event, inertial, glove, tactile or capacitive sensing
themes.what_papers_do: These papers estimate 3D hand pose, and sometimes the shape of a grasped object hidden by the hand, from a non-RGB or additional modality. The modalities are depth images and point-cloud sequences, event streams fused with RGB, sparse hand-worn IMUs, IMU, potentiometer or capacitive gloves, vision plus distributed tactile sensing, and capacitive sensing on object surfaces. Method mix: diffusion or graph transformers on point clouds (HandDiff, HandDAGT, UST-Hand), keypoint-level RGB-depth fusion, probabilistic visual-inertial filtering, differentiable MANO calibration for gloves, and prior distillation into sparse-IMU models. Several are hardware papers whose aim is ground-truth annotation rather than estimation.

themes.name: Hand-object contact, pressure and force estimation and contact-event localization
themes.what_papers_do: These papers estimate dense per-vertex hand contact, pressure or 3D force on hand and object meshes, from a single image or a video, sometimes fused with sEMG. Others localize the frames of touch and release in egocentric video, or estimate dense hand-object interaction fields (the SHOW3D challenge). Method mix: supervised regressors with imbalance-aware losses (HACO), video models (HOPE), posture-plus-sEMG fusion (PiMForce), zero-shot VLM or MLLM prompting (EgoLoc, ContactPrompt), and stereo attention networks for interaction fields. Labels come from pressure pads, tactile gloves, instrumented objects, simulation or multi-view capture. Several rows are the datasets that supply those labels (EgoPressure, EgoTactile, HT-Bench, FEEL, DyTact).

themes.what_papers_do: These papers track the 6-DoF pose of a manipulated, often unseen, object through hand occlusion, or recover an articulated object's parts and joints from a video of a person operating it. The hand is used as a cue or a constraint. themes.name: Capture systems, datasets and benchmarks with 3D hand-object ground truth
themes.what_papers_do: These rows build capture rigs and annotation pipelines that produce 3D hand (MANO or UmeTrack) and object pose or mesh ground truth, then release datasets and challenge benchmarks. Ground truth comes from four sources: optical marker mocap plus multi-view RGB, dense markerless multi-view RGB with model fitting (12 to 70 cameras), multi-view RGB-D (Azure Kinect class) optimization, or headset on-device tracking. Recent sets add bimanual long-horizon tasks, articulated objects, text, gaze, force and in-the-wild egocentric capture.

themes.name: Static grasp synthesis on object geometry (contact-, affordance-, taxonomy- or language-conditioned)
themes.what_papers_do: Given an object point cloud or mesh (sometimes a single-view scene point cloud or RGB-D), these papers generate a static MANO or dexterous robot-hand grasp. No camera observation of a human is involved. Method mix: diffusion or latent diffusion is the majority (UGG, FastGrasp, MGD, SNS-Grasp, AffordGrasp, Text2Grasp, ClickDiff, NL2Contact). Others use part-decomposed VQ-VAE tokens (SemGrasp, DVQ-VAE) or fine-tuned multimodal LLMs and VLMs (Multi-GraspLLM, DexVLG). A predicted contact or affordance map usually comes first, followed by contact or penetration optimization. Robot-hand variants are checked in simulation and on a few real grasps.

themes.name: Hand-object motion sequence synthesis (text-, trajectory-, gaze-, mass- or audio-conditioned; kinematic diffusion and physics RL)
themes.what_papers_do: These papers generate temporal sequences of one- or two-hand (sometimes whole-body) motion interacting with rigid or articulated objects. Conditions include text, an object trajectory or geometry, gaze, mass, music or audio, or an egocentric image. Method mix: staged diffusion or flow matching (contact first, then motion) is the core (Text2HOI, DiffH2O, LatentHOI, BimArt, HO-Flow, JointHOI, MACS, TOUCH). Others use VQ tokenizers with language models (HOIGPT, CLUTCH, SynHLMA, OpenHOI with a 3D MLLM) or RL policies in physics simulation (GraspXL, ArtiGrasp, guitar playing, ForceGrip). Interaction transfer and motion clean-up (correspondence fields, MOCHI) fill out the set.

themes.what_papers_do: Conditional image or video diffusion models generate hand or hand-object images and videos from 3D hand and object geometry, keypoints, sparse 3D joints, text or exocentric views. The 3D quantity is the conditioning signal, not the output; SViMo is the exception and co-generates 3D motion. Method mix: about 8 rows synthesize labelled images to train 3D hand estimators or detectors (HOIDiffusion, HandBooster/HandBooster+, AttentionHand, SesaHand, AnyHand, HOGSA, the synthetic-to-real gap analysis). About 15 generate or edit HOI video, including egocentric world models (ManiVideo, HOI-Swap, TASTE-Rob, HVG-3D, HandsOnWorld). Glove2Hand translates sensing-glove video into bare-hand video so that glove signals become ground truth.

sensing_shift:
Both analysts matched keywords in the free-text sensing field of all 354 rows. They used different keyword rules, so their counts differ in level but agree in direction; both sets are reported as approximate.

Video input grew strongly. Analyst 1 counted 26 of 99 rows in 2024, 47 of 128 in 2025 and 56 of 117 in 2026. Analyst 2 counted 24, 40 and 48 with a narrower rule. Either way the subfield is moving from single images to sequences.

Egocentric sensing grew from 17 to 34 to 41 rows (the analysts agree exactly). The egocentric camera is now usually a moving head-mounted device with SLAM poses (Aria, Quest 3, Vision Pro) rather than a static chest camera. Lifting estimates to world space under camera motion is new in 2025-2026 (merged theme of 8 rows, 0 in 2024).

Multi-view and RGB-D fell as shares of yearly rows. Multi-view: analyst 1 measured about 13 to 7 percent; analyst 2 counted 21, 21 and 14 rows. RGB-D or depth: about 11 to 7 percent (analyst 1); 14, 17 and 10 rows (analyst 2).

Where active depth and calibrated multi-camera rigs remain, they mostly produce ground truth, not test-time input. Of the 35 dataset rows, 11 mention RGB-D or depth and 28 mention multi-view (merged classification). The other remaining use is the robot side of human-to-robot pipelines, where 16 of 61 rows mention RGB-D, depth or point clouds. Only about 9 estimation rows outside those two themes take depth at test time: 4 depth hand-pose rows, the single-RGB-D hand-object SDF row, the transparent-object row, PickScan, HOIC, and several object-side trackers.

The merged object-side theme is the one estimation theme where RGB-D or stereo is common, at 5 of 9 rows. Pure 3D-input rows (grasp and motion synthesis with no camera) fell from 18 to 17 to 8 (analyst 2).

Wearable and contact sensing is rising, as both analysts found. IMU, tactile, pressure, force and sEMG mentions went from about 11 to 15 to 18 rows (analyst 2). These sensors serve mainly as ground truth for contact and pressure, for occluded finger pose (Glove2Hand, FLiPo, AVI-HT) and for robot transfer, not as inference input.

Consumer XR headsets have become capture devices whose on-device hand tracking is treated as labels (EgoDex, HOT3D, SHOW3D).

The analysts also agree, from reading contribution text rather than the sensing field, that by 2026 the de facto front end is a stack of frozen foundation models. HaMeR, WiLoR or HaWoR handle hands; DUSt3R, VGGT, MoGe or CUT3R handle camera and depth; SAM or SAM3D handle objects, alongside image-to-3D models.
dataset_ecosystem:
The counts below are substring matches on the datasets field of all 354 rows, rechecked by the reconciler: ARCTIC 24, DexYCB 22, HO3D/HO-3D 22, GRAB 16, OakInk/OakInk2 16, H2O 14, FreiHAND 9, HOT3D 9, Ego-Exo4D 8, HOI4D 7. Analyst 1 counted DexYCB at 23 and Ego-Exo4D at about 9; analyst 2 counted OakInk at 13. These are small spelling and rule differences. Further down are Ego4D (about 7), EPIC-Kitchens (about 6), InterHand2.6M and AssemblyHands (5 each), and TACO and DexGraspNet (about 4 each).

Usage splits by problem:
- Single-image hand and hand-object estimation: FreiHAND, DexYCB, HO3D.
- Template-free video reconstruction: HO3D and the HANDS 2024/2025 ARCTIC category-agnostic track. That track is scored with hand-relative Chamfer CD_h on 9 rigid-object test clips (per the rows), and it is where Gaussian-splatting entries compete.
- Grasp and motion synthesis: trains on GRAB, OakInk and ARCTIC.
- Egocentric work: HOT3D (also used in BOP 2024 H3 and the HANDS MegoTrack challenge per the rows), Ego-Exo4D, HoloAssist, EPIC, and the new SHOW3D interaction-field challenge (ECCV 2026).
- Contact and force: EgoPressure, EgoTactile, HT-Bench, FEEL and instrumented objects.

New 2024-2026 datasets in the rows: HOT3D, GigaHands, OakInk2, TACO, HOGraspNet, ParaHome, HUMOTO, HO-Cap, OphNet-3D, EPFL-Smart-Kitchen, SHOW3D, Ego-1K, HD-EPIC, EgoPressure, and robot-oriented corpora (EgoDex, DexCanvas, OpenEgo, HRDexDB, ACE-Data-0).

The rows' type field marks 52 rows as dataset and 6 as benchmark. The analysts' 53 and about 90 "introduce data" counts came from different matching rules; the type-field count is the cleaner one.

Ground truth comes from four kinds of source:
1. Optical marker mocap plus multi-view RGB: ARCTIC, OakInk2, TACO, HOT3D, HUMOTO. Accurate, but markers alter appearance.
2. Dense markerless multi-view RGB with model fitting: GigaHands, MANUS, ParaHome, FurElise, HMDO. Accuracy is self-reported.
3. Multi-view RGB-D (Kinect class) optimization: HOGraspNet, InterCap, HO-Cap, OphNet-3D, ADL4D, HOH, EgoPressure.
4. On-device headset tracking or pseudo-labels from HaMeR/HaWoR-type trackers, used mainly in robot-learning corpora (EgoDex, MINT, the hand-VLA corpus). A growing share of training data is therefore labelled by the same estimators the field evaluates, with unquantified error.

Synthetic rendering (ObMan, POV-Surgery, AnyHand) is a minor fifth source.

About 107 rows (30 percent) name no dataset in the abstract-derived field, so per-theme dataset rankings are soft and understate how concentrated evaluation is.
saturated:
1. Generative grasp and hand-object synthesis from object geometry and text. It totals 53 rows: 23 static-grasp and 30 motion-synthesis rows in the merged map. The formulation is nearly identical across papers: contact or affordance map, then MANO or dexterous pose, then optional physics refinement. Evaluation reuses GRAB, OakInk and DexGraspNet. Language-guided dexterous grasping in particular has many near-variants (SemGrasp, GYS, DexVLG, AffordDexGrasp, Text2Grasp, Multi-GraspLLM, SNS-Grasp, AffordGrasp, ClickDiff). Static grasp synthesis is already falling in raw counts (12, 8, 3) and as a share of yearly rows, which suggests the community treats it as saturated. Motion synthesis is flat (9, 13, 8).

2. Single-image hand mesh regression after HaMeR and WiLoR. Rows mostly swap the backbone or decoder (Mamba, discrete tokens, VQ masked modelling, MAE or contrastive pre-training, MoGe or VGGT adapters) and re-benchmark on FreiHAND, DexYCB and HO3D with small margins.

3. Template-free monocular hand-object video reconstruction converged in 2025-2026 on Gaussian splatting plus foundation-model initialization. Five HANDS challenge reports and several arXiv 2026 papers compete on the same ARCTIC 9-clip and HO3D setting.

4. Egocentric 2D/3D hand-trajectory forecasting with latent diffusion (MADiff, Uni-Hand, MMTwin, Diff-IP2D, EER) produces many near-variants on EPIC, EgoPAT3D and H2O.

5. Human-video-to-robot transfer is the largest and fastest-growing theme: 61 rows, 11 then 25 then 25 per year. Its perception pipeline (HaMeR/WiLoR/HaWoR plus a 6-DoF object tracker, retargeting, residual RL) is becoming boilerplate. Each paper evaluates on its own few robot tasks without a shared benchmark or reported pose error, so comparison across papers is nearly impossible.
rare_or_absent:
1. RGB-D or depth as the test-time input for 3D hand-object tracking. In the merged classification only about 9 estimation rows use it: 4 depth hand-pose rows, which estimate the hand only; the single-RGB-D hand-object SDF row (ECCV 2024); the transparent-object depth-restoration row; PickScan (single RGB-D video); HOIC (single depth plus physics); and RGB-D or stereo object trackers (POGS, ArtiPoint, FunREC). Robot pipelines such as OKAMI and DemoBot use RGB-D, but they consume the hand estimate rather than evaluate it.

2. Online multi-view calibrated RGB-D tracking of bimanual manipulation. It is essentially absent as a method; such rigs appear only as offline annotation pipelines (HO-Cap, HOGraspNet, InterCap, ADL4D, OphNet-3D, EgoPressure).

3. Metric, absolute-scale accuracy of hands and objects in a fixed world frame. It is rarely the headline. Most rows report root-relative MPJPE or hand-relative Chamfer. EgoForce, HGGT and the 8 world-grounded rows are the exceptions, and video object reconstructions are up to scale.

4. Long-duration causal tracking with re-initialization and drift reporting, and object 6-DoF stability through full grasp occlusion. These are rarely evaluated. ComPose, MGS-Track and POGS are the main object-tracking rows.

5. Runtime or latency. Few rows report it: 3D-AMTA, QORT-Former, REWIND, WiLoR and HandOS-type efficiency claims. None report it for full hand-object tracking on real-time hardware.

6. Accuracy of the ground truth itself. It is rarely quantified, especially for markerless and headset pseudo-labels. FLiPo and FSGlove are validated against mocap and SHOWMe has sub-millimetre scans, but these are the exceptions.

7. Uncertainty estimates and failure detection for hand-object pose. These are almost absent, apart from probabilistic or multi-hypothesis hand regressors (cascaded diffusion, MaskHand confidence, HandBooster+).

8. Narrow object and interaction classes. Deformable objects (HMDO, ViTaM-D, a soft-object poster), transparent objects (2 rows), surgical tools (OphNet-3D, POV-Surgery) and human-to-human handover or multi-person interaction (HOH, ADL4D, HO-Cap, MOCHI) each have only a handful of rows.

9. Arm, forearm and upper-limb kinematics coupled to the hands. These are nearly absent, with EgoForce and Hand4Whole++ as the main exceptions.

10. Wearable-plus-vision fusion. Fusion for object pose, as opposed to hand pose, is nearly absent. RGB-D fused with IMU or tactile data for hand-object tracking does not appear at all; existing fusion rows are RGB plus IMU.

11. Physical-validity metrics (penetration, simulator executability). They appear only in the physics and synthesis themes and are not standard in estimation papers.

12. Cross-dataset generalization protocols and negative results. They are rare; the CVPR 2025 synthetic-to-real gap analysis is one exception.

13. Propagation of upstream hand-pose error into downstream robot success. No retargeting paper measures it.
notes:
The reconciler read all 354 rows and assigned every row to exactly one of 16 merged themes (15 named themes plus other). Counts and by_year values are exact for those assignments. The file has 354 JSON lines; wc reports 353 because the last line has no trailing newline. 10 rows dated 2022-2023 are counted in theme totals but not in by_year: 9 in datasets and 1 survey in other. Yearly totals are 99 (2024), 128 (2025) and 117 (2026). Working files: scratchpad/rec_s1.py and rec_s1_theme.json, with codes T01-T16 in the theme order above. They build on analyst 1's scratchpad/s1_assign.txt with explicit overrides.

How the two lenses were merged, and why:
(a) Problem-lens cuts were kept where they separate research lines better than the method lens. The method lens grouped avatars, splatting-based video reconstruction and splatting object trackers into one Gaussian-splatting theme of 26 rows. That theme was dissolved: avatars (11) stay their own theme, splatting reconstructions go to video HO reconstruction, and POGS/MGS-Track go to object-side tracking. Splatting is recorded as a method mix inside each.
(b) Method-lens cuts were adopted in three places:
- Generative synthesis (problem lens 53) was split into static grasp synthesis (23) and HOI motion synthesis (30). Grasp-only work is declining while motion synthesis is flat, so the split shows a real difference.
- World-grounded moving-camera motion was made its own new theme (8, all 2025-2026).
- Physics-aware refinement became its own theme (9). The problem lens had buried it in video reconstruction and the method lens had merged it with contact estimation. Its inputs, its consumers and its use of simulators differ from both.
(c) Contact, pressure and force estimation stays separate from physics refinement (17 rows).

Themes where the analysts disagreed by more than 30 percent were recounted against the rows:
- Video hand-object reconstruction: 34 vs 17. Merged 25, after moving out 9 physics rows (19, 151, 233, 241, 248 plus HandyPriors 178), 2 world-grounded rows (WHOLE, EgoGrasp) and FunREC (to object-side).
- Temporal hand motion vs world-grounded: 14 vs 8. Merged world-grounded 8. The 5 remaining temporal hand-only rows (low-res video, prior-aware temporal, ConTrack, UniHand, the generative temporal transformer) moved to the hand-only theme. MS-MANO, intuitive-physics diffusion and PAD-Hand moved to physics.
- Non-RGB sensors: 13 vs 17. Merged 14 (analyst 1's 13 plus surface capacitive sensing). PiMForce stays in contact, the transparent-object RGB-D row stays in single-frame HO, and EHoA stays in other.
- Object-side: 8 vs not a theme. Merged 9 (adds FunREC).
- Contact: 16 vs 20. The method-lens 20 includes physics refinement. Merged 17 (adds FEEL).

Themes within 30 percent were also adjusted:
- Datasets: 43 vs 35. Merged 35. Six robot-learning corpora (EgoDex, VTDexManip, Kaiwu, HRDexDB, ACE-Data-0, DexCanvas) moved to robot transfer, Glove2Hand to image/video synthesis, and FEEL to contact.
- Robot transfer: 51 vs 63. Merged 61, adding those 6 corpora plus 4 robot-motivated affordance rows: 2HandedAfforder, Learning Precise Affordances, GLOVER++, part-level affordance grounding.
- Forecasting: 19 vs 15. Merged 15, after removing those affordance rows.
- Hand-only RGB: 25 vs 27. Merged 30, including the temporal rows above.
- Other: 20 vs 27. Merged 19. The method lens had put articulation and contact-timing rows in other; they are now in the object-side and contact themes.

Contradictions resolved:
1. Dataset trend. Analyst 1 said stable (12, 12, 10) and analyst 2 said falling (12, 11, 3). Merged is 12, 10, 4: most 2026 data rows are robot-learning corpora, now counted under robot transfer. The trend is labelled falling with a caveat. NeurIPS 2026 Datasets and Benchmarks and other late-2026 venues are mostly absent from the inventory, a statement that rests on knowledge of the venue calendar, not on the rows. So part of the decline is coverage.
2. Non-RGB sensors trend. Analyst 1 said stable and analyst 2 said rising. Merged 4, 3, 7 is labelled rising, but it is a small absolute change.
3. Datasets-introduced count: 53 vs about 90. The type field gives 52 dataset plus 6 benchmark rows; the larger figure comes from a looser text match.
4. RGB-D share: the analysts' row counts differ because of their keyword rules, but both show a decline.

Caveats:
- 2026 is a partial year, so absolute 2026 drops (static grasp 3, datasets 4) should be read alongside shares. Static grasp synthesis falls from 12 percent to 6 percent to 3 percent of yearly rows, a real decline.
- 48 rows are arXiv-only, concentrated in 2026, and they inflate the rising themes (video reconstruction, world-grounded, robot transfer). 15 rows are workshop or challenge reports.
- OakInk2 appears twice (CVPR 2024, rows at positions 17 and 304); both are counted. Two different GHOST papers exist: CVPR 2026 Findings and an ICCV 2025 workshop report.
- Several rows are title-only, so their placement is low-confidence: HandSCS, ConTrack, PCIE_Pose, Keystate-Driven, the soft-object poster, Get a Grip.
- The static versus motion split of HO-Flow and JointHOI rests on the reconciler's knowledge, not on the rows.
- The robot-transfer sub-split (about 27 / 8 / 17 / 9) is an approximate reading, not a verified tally.

Scope: about 114 rows (static grasp 23, motion synthesis 30, robot transfer 61) consume rather than estimate hand-object pose; their tags also carry S3 or S6. The estimation core is about 135 rows: hand-only, single-frame HO, video HO, world-grounded, physics, sensors, contact and object-side. With datasets added it is about 170.

Sources: statements that HaMeR/WiLoR/HaWoR are the de facto front ends, and about the ARCTIC CD_h and SHOW3D challenges, come from the rows. Statements about the usual evaluation sets of world-grounded methods and about FoundationPose-style trackers in robot pipelines rest on knowledge, not on the rows.

No repository files were edited.

themes.name: Kinematic HOI motion generation from text, object geometry or trajectories (no sensor input at inference)
themes.what_papers_do: These papers generate SMPL-X body motion (sometimes with MANO hands) together with object 6-DoF motion, or a static human-object configuration. The conditions are text, an object mesh, waypoints, an object trajectory, audio or a 3D scene, and the models are trained on mocap or multi-view fits. The methods mix as follows. Most rows are conditional diffusion with contact or distance-field guidance (CG-HOI, CHOIS, NIFTY, Guiding HOI). Variants use kinematic-chain graphs (ChainHOI), masked VQ tokens (HOIMask), latent consistency (GRIP), asynchronous diffusion forcing (Unleashing Guidance), driver-responder dynamics losses (HOI-Dyn) or noise optimization across coupled body and hand models (CoDA). A zero-shot branch uses LLM planning with pretrained motion or 2D diffusion priors (InterDreamer, InteractAnything, AvatarGO, InterFusion). A human-scene branch includes LINGO, SceneMI, Space Occupancy, InfBaGel and Uni-Inter. The theme also holds generation-oriented data consolidation (InterAct, Semantic-HOI/F-HOI) and diffusion-prior cleanup of noisy captures (MOCHI).

themes.what_papers_do: From one RGB image (sparse views in Ins-HOI), these papers estimate an SMPL(-X) body and the object's 6-DoF pose or full shape. Methods fall into three lines. Feed-forward regression with explicit contact or graph heads: CONTHO, HOI-TG, CrossHOI. Diffusion priors with physical or score guidance: HDM/ProciGen, ScoreHOI. Optimization against dense contact or proximity fields: PICO, Open3DHOI, LEXIS, GraspHOI. The 2026 rows drop object templates in favour of large 3D reconstruction models or shared triplanes (MILO, unified triplane), add text or texture (TeHOR, ReGenHOI), and recover finger-level grasps (GraspHOI).

themes.name: Physics-simulated humanoid controllers that perform or imitate HOI
themes.what_papers_do: These papers train RL policies that make a simulated humanoid, often with dexterous hands, grasp, carry, rearrange, reach or play ball with objects. The methods mix as follows. Unified HOI imitation rewards: SkillMimic, SkillMimic-V2. Teacher-student distillation over imperfect mocap: InterMimic, MaskedManipulator, HumanVLA. Masked-constraint inpainting: MaskedMimic. Pretrained motion representations: Omnigrasp. Multi-agent RL: CooHOI. Learning from brief walking references: the CVPR 2025 reaching row. Real-time reactive planning with tracking: Human-X. LLM or VLM-designed plans and rewards: Human-Level Instructions, VLM-Guided Motion Policy. Mimicking-Bench supplies a benchmark. Mocap is the demonstration source, and physics is used to repair it.

themes.name: Dense contact, affordance and interaction-field estimation and representation
themes.what_papers_do: These papers predict or represent where interaction happens instead of full poses: vertex-level body contact, object affordance regions, orientation and proximity distributions, and cross-object correspondence for transferring an interaction. The inputs are an image (DECO, LEMON, InteractVLM, Pi-HOC), egocentric video plus head motion (EgoChoir), object geometry with samples from 2D, video or 3D generative models (ComA, DAViD, H2OFlow) or captured motion (Contacts from Motion). VolumetricSMPL and the SIGGRAPH correspondence field supply contact, collision and transfer representations for downstream fitting. The methods are transformers and VLM- or foundation-model-feature lifting for image inputs, and distillation from generative models when labels are scarce.

themes.name: Monocular-video 4D HOI reconstruction (body sequence plus object trajectory)
themes.what_papers_do: From one RGB video, often handheld or internet footage with a moving camera, these papers recover a time-consistent SMPL-X sequence and the object's 6-DoF trajectory, increasingly at metric scale in a world frame. The methods mix as follows. Optimization seeded by foundation-model pose hypotheses with render-and-compare: CARI4D. Foundation-model-stabilized SfM: RHINO. Human-in-the-loop sparse contact annotation for scalable data: 4DHOISolver, HAT-4D. Physics-simulator or RL refinement against floating and penetration: Recovering Physically Plausible HOI, Real2Sim in HOI. A feed-forward spatio-temporal transformer with an object template: THO, which claims 31.5 FPS. Lifting with a 2D motion diffusion model: AnyLift. themes.name: Human-to-robot and humanoid transfer of whole-body demonstrations
themes.what_papers_do: These papers turn human demonstrations into robot or humanoid behaviour. The demonstrations are one RGB-D video, casual phone video or mocap. The pipelines reconstruct the human, object and environment, retarget while preserving object and contact relations, and train or execute a policy. The methods mix as follows: object-aware retargeting (OKAMI); real-to-sim-to-real RL from reconstructed human and scene (VideoMimic); safety value functions (SafeMimic); interaction-preserving retargeting optimization (OmniRetarget); adversarial imitation of decomposed primitives on a HOI graph (IROS 2025); learned interaction translation (IROS 2024); and capture with contact and force sensing for a soft robot hand (bathing). Reconstruction is a component, not the evaluated output.

themes.name: Body-worn and non-camera HOI sensing (IMUs, head-wrist wearables, LiDAR)
themes.what_papers_do: These papers estimate body pose and object trajectory, or human motion in large spaces, from sensors other than external cameras. I'M HOI fuses one RGB camera with one object IMU. IMU-HOI fuses sparse body IMUs with an object IMU and infers contact probabilistically. ECHO runs a tri-variate diffusion over head and wrist poses from glasses and a watch. HiSC4D jointly optimizes body IMUs with a head-mounted LiDAR. An arXiv 2026 row estimates pose from LiDAR point clouds using HOI cues. In every row, contact is treated as a latent variable inferred from sparse signals.

sensing_shift: Both analysts agree, and the rows support it: test-time input for whole-body HOI estimation moved from benchmark images and controlled capture to unconstrained monocular RGB. In 2024, estimation rows reconstruct body plus object from a single RGB image trained and tested on BEHAVE and InterCap (CONTHO, HDM, LEMON). The capture rigs of that year combine dense RGB with object IMUs or markers (HOI-M3, I'M HOI, OAKINK2). In 2025, single-image work moves to in-the-wild, open-vocabulary images using foundation and VLM priors (Open3DHOI, PICO, InteractVLM). In 2026 a monocular-video 4D HOI cluster appears: 7 of its 8 rows are from 2026 (CARI4D, RHINO, AnyLift, HAT-4D, THO, Real2Sim in HOI, Recovering Physically Plausible HOI). These rows feature moving or handheld cameras, metric world grounding, and physics or Real2Sim refinement. Missing geometry now comes from foundation models rather than depth sensors: Hunyuan3D and SAM 3D Objects in MILO, MASt3R and CUT3R in HAMSt3R and Human3R, and monocular depth in PhySIC and CRISP. A smaller second shift goes toward body-worn sensing with no external camera: object IMUs (I'M HOI 2024, IMU-HOI 2026), glasses plus watch (ECHO 2026), and LiDAR (HiSC4D 2024, an arXiv 2026 row). Capture datasets moved from 4-6 Kinect RGB-D views (BEHAVE, InterCap, HOH, CHAIRS) to dense RGB domes (HODome 76 views, ParaHome 70 cameras), optical mocap with RGB (HIMO, HUMOTO, TRUMANS), and ego-exo rigs with gaze, audio or tactile streams (Ego-Exo4D, InterVLA, ACE-Data-0, SABER). Two RGB-D datasets do still appear in 2025: EPFL-Smart-Kitchen with nine RGB-D cameras, and Intend to Move. Sensed depth has nearly left the method side. Ten rows name RGB-D or sensed depth in the sensing field, verified by a scan plus reading: BEHAVE 2022, CHAIRS 2023, HOH 2023, DNA-Rendering 2023, InterCap twice in 2024, THOR (reuse of BEHAVE captures), OKAMI 2024, EPFL-Smart-Kitchen 2025 and Intend to Move 2025. Of these, OKAMI is the only 2024-2026 method that takes a sensed RGB-D video at runtime, and it uses it for robot imitation, not metric HOI tracking. Generation, physics-control and video-generation rows total 50 of 149, and they use no sensor at inference.
dataset_ecosystem: Dataset name counts below are verified by a substring scan of the datasets field. BEHAVE is the most-named dataset: 12 rows. Next come InterCap (7), OMOMO/FullBodyManip (6), GRAB (4), DAMON (4), and Ego-Exo4D, CHAIRS, PROX and RICH (3 each). Ground truth is of three kinds. (1) SMPL(-H/X) and object-template fits to multi-view RGB(-D) or RGB domes: BEHAVE, InterCap, CHAIRS, HOH, HODome, HOI-M3. Their accuracy is bounded by the fitting, and their own error is seldom reported. The detail that BEHAVE uses 4 Kinect views and InterCap 6 rests on analyst knowledge, not on the rows. (2) Optical marker mocap: OMOMO, GRAB, HIMO, HUMOTO, TRUMANS, OAKINK2, InterVLA. Generation and humanoid-control rows train and evaluate mostly on these sets and on the consolidated InterAct. (3) Pseudo-ground-truth built in the wild: annotated contact with mesh retrieval or fitting (DAMON, PICO-db, Open3DHOI), human-in-the-loop sparse contact on internet video (Open4DHOI), procedural synthetic data (ProciGen), and samples from generative models (ComA, DAViD, H2OFlow). Datasets new in 2024-2026 within these rows: HOI-M3, IMHD2, OAKINK2, TRUMANS, BOTH57M, HIMO, Semantic-HOI, LINGO, Ego-Exo4D, InterCap (IJCV journal version), CORE4D, ParaHome, HUMOTO, InterVLA, InterAct, EPFL-Smart-Kitchen-30, I2M, PMR, AssemblyHands-X, Open3DHOI, PICO-db, Open4DHOI, ProciGen, 3DIR, SparseHOI-5K, ACE-Data-0, SABER, and several basketball/BallPlay sets. The direction is toward more objects, multiple people, articulated objects, finger-level hands, text, and ego/exo views. Coverage is thin: 53 of 149 rows have 'not stated', 'not named', 'not checked' or 'none' in the datasets field, verified by regex. Analyst A gave 51 with a narrower pattern. Dataset use in 2026 rows in particular cannot be confirmed from the inventory.
saturated: Kinematic text- or condition-to-HOI motion generation is the most crowded line: 33 of 149 rows, 12 in 2024 and 16 in 2025. Papers differ mainly in the guidance or coupling device: contact maps, distance or interaction fields, kinematic-chain graphs, masked tokens, asynchronous noise, LLM planners. They report penetration and contact metrics on the same few mocap sets (OMOMO, BEHAVE, GRAB, CHAIRS), and no row validates against independently captured physical interaction. Physics-based simulated-humanoid HOI imitation (14 rows) is crowded with close 'mimic' variants: InterMimic, SkillMimic, SkillMimic-V2, MaskedMimic, MaskedManipulator, WristMimic. These recur on the same benchmark tasks, grasp-and-carry and ball play. Single-image body-plus-object reconstruction (16 rows) is incremental on BEHAVE and InterCap. The field responded by moving to in-the-wild, template-free and large-reconstruction-model settings rather than chasing BEHAVE numbers. Dataset releases (26 rows) keep coming, each adding one axis (multi-person, articulated, egocentric, text), while evaluation protocols do not converge. Two claims rest on analyst knowledge, not the rows: that BEHAVE-style object-pose errors are dominated by symmetric objects and fitting noise, and that the benchmark is therefore hard to read.
rare_or_absent: (1) Test-time RGB-D or depth-camera input for whole-body plus object tracking. Among the 140 rows dated 2024-2026, only OKAMI uses a single RGB-D video, and only for robot imitation. BEHAVE's 2022 single-RGB-D tracker is the last metric HOI tracker of this kind in the rows, although the main benchmarks were captured with Kinects. Calibration, synchronization and occlusion handling across several depth sensors are not treated as research problems in any 2024-2026 row. (2) Fiducial or marker-based object pose (ArUco, AprilTag) as a cheap object-pose source does not appear. The only marker row is the IROS 2024 optical-marker object-and-wrench algorithm. (3) Bimanual whole-body HOI estimation with finger-level hands on one object is rare in methods: GraspHOI and CoDA. It lives mostly in datasets: OAKINK2, BOTH57M, ParaHome, AssemblyHands-X, HOH. (4) Real-time or online capture: only THO (31.5 FPS claimed) and Human3R (online single pass) claim it. (5) Metric accuracy against independent ground truth, for example marker mocap as reference for markerless or monocular estimates. Also absent: reporting the error of the ground truth itself, cross-dataset generalization studies, uncertainty estimates, and per-sequence failure analysis. The new 4D monocular theme has no shared benchmark named in the rows. (6) Force, wrench and tactile sensing: only the IROS 2024 wrench row, the RSS 2026 bathing capture and ACE-Data-0's tactile gloves. Object mass and dynamics appear only in physics-refinement rows. (7) Deformable objects are absent. Articulated objects appear in only a handful of rows (CHAIRS, HUMOTO, ParaHome, CoDA, VLM-Guided Motion Policy). (8) Robotics venues barely do HOI capture or reconstruction. Their 15 rows (CoRL 3, RSS 2, ICRA 3, IROS 7) are transfer, forecasting and recognition, contact from motion, one capture-processing row and one rendering row (MM-GS). (9) Outdoor and large-space HOI capture is limited to HiSC4D and PMR.
notes: Reconciliation method: I re-read all 149 rows (ids 8 to 1563; the file has 148 newline-terminated lines plus a final row) and assigned each row to exactly one merged theme. All counts and by_year values come from a script over those assignments. Counts sum to 149: 33+26+16+14+11+8+8+8+7+6+5+3+4. by_year covers only 2024-2026 (140 rows: 44, 56, 40). The 9 pre-2024 rows sit outside by_year: 7 in capture (BEHAVE, RICH, COUCH from 2022; CHAIRS, NeuralDome, OMOMO, HOH from 2023), 1 in rendering (DNA-Rendering 2023) and 1 in contact (DECO 2023). The two analysts (A problem lens, B method lens) cut the rows almost identically. Twelve of thirteen themes correspond one-to-one, so the merged map keeps those 12 problem cuts and folds B's method descriptions into each theme as a method mix. Disagreements and how I resolved them: (a) 'other' (A 5, B 3; more than 30 percent apart, re-checked). VolumetricSMPL (250) moves to the contact theme with B, because it is a contact and collision representation. The amodal completion row (244) stays in 'other' with A, against B, because it is a 2D inpainting step, not 3D reconstruction; so single-image reconstruction is 16 (A) rather than 17 (B). The occluded-human paper (425) and the two surveys stay in 'other'. Final count: 4. (b) Contact (A 9, B 11; 22 percent apart, re-checked anyway). It ends at 11. VolumetricSMPL is added, and so is the SIGGRAPH 2024 correspondence-field interaction-transfer row (539), which A had in generation. (c) MOCHI (565): A put it in capture, B in generation. I follow B: it is a diffusion-prior motion-enhancement method, not a capture rig. The generation count stays 33 because 539 leaves and 565 enters relative to A. (d) IROS 2024 optical-marker object-augmentation row (898): A put it in capture, B in non-camera sensors. I follow A, because it post-processes a marker mocap rig, so capture is 26 and sensors 5. (e) A said the transfer theme was 'stable'; B said 'rising' (2, 4, 2 by year). I keep 'stable', because the year counts do not support rising. (f) For the contact theme by year, A gave 4/2/2 and B 5/3/2; the recount with the merged assignment is 5/3/2. (g) A said 9 rows mention RGB-D. A sensing-field scan plus reading finds 10 rows naming RGB-D or sensed depth, plus 2 with estimated monocular depth. The difference is DNA-Rendering ('with depth'). CORE4D's RGB-D is not in its row, so it rests on analyst knowledge. Duplicates are counted as listed: InterCap (ids 1083 and 1563, both capture) and VideoMimic (ids 640 and 1338, both transfer), which overstates each of those themes by one. Of the 149 rows, 19 are arXiv, plus one 3DV row and one ICCV-workshop row, all outside the target venues. 2026 venue coverage in the inventory is partial (no NeurIPS, SIGGRAPH Asia or ICCV 2026), so the 2025-to-2026 drop in generation and physics control should not be read as decline. Borderline assignments: SceneMI and the human-scene generation rows are in generation, not human-scene reconstruction. PhysHO is in rendering, not 4D video. Ins-HOI (sparse-view) is in single-image reconstruction. LEXIS is in single-image reconstruction, although its main device is a proximity field. InteractVLM is in contact. WristMimic and Human-X are in physics control. ACE-Data-0 and SABER are in capture, not transfer. OMOMO is in capture as a dataset row. The IROS 2024 rows have thin metadata ('not checked'), so their placement is less certain. Statements resting on analyst knowledge rather than the rows: how BEHAVE and InterCap ground truth was produced, which benchmarks the 2026 monocular-video papers use, and BEHAVE error sources. Relevance to bimanual RGB-D object handling: the closest rows are BEHAVE (2022), InterCap (IJCV 2024), HOH (2023), CHAIRS (2023), OKAMI (CoRL 2024) and AssemblyHands-X. The 2024-2026 method mainstream has moved to monocular RGB with foundation-model priors, and RGB-D survives mainly as a dataset-capture modality. No repository files were edited. themes.name: Egocentric and moving-camera two-hand motion: world-space 4D recovery, headset multi-view tracking and forecasting
themes.what_papers_do: Estimate both hands' 3D motion over time from head-worn or moving cameras. Three method groups make up the theme. The largest (6 rows: Dyn-HaMR, HaWoR, EgoAllo, StableHand, the video-diffusion paper, MEgoVista) recovers gravity-aligned world-frame trajectories by separating hand motion from SLAM camera motion and infilling occluded or out-of-view frames with diffusion or flow-matching priors or a repurposed video diffusion model. Calibrated multi-view headset tracking and view adaptation account for 4 rows (UmeTrack, two MegoTrack challenge reports, Single-to-Dual-View). Forecasting of future bimanual motion from an image or egocentric video, using body pose as a cue, accounts for 2. The remaining 2 rows are in-context egocentric reconstruction (EgoHandICL) and a temporal pose-and-action transformer.

The usual tools are residual learning over a kinematic imitator, virtual object controllers with a curriculum, or wrist guidance plus RL finger control. Related rows synthesise physically plausible bimanual grasping and articulation (ArtiGrasp), clean noisy multi-person captures (MOCHI), or evaluate retargeting metrics. The research problem is the gap between kinematic mocap and physically executable motion, not perception.

Egocentric Aria, Vision Pro or wearable-camera data is used for policy pretraining (EgoMimic, H-RDT, EgoBridge, Humanoid Policy ~ Human Policy, DexRoam). themes.name: Bimanual robot policy architectures, simulation benchmarks and demonstration augmentation (no human-hand perception)
themes.what_papers_do: Learn two-arm or two-dexterous-hand robot policies from robot teleoperation data or RL. Evaluation is defined by simulated benchmarks (Bi-DexHands, RoboTwin 1 and 2, BiGym, TWIN, DexGarmentLab, HumanoidGen). sensing_shift:
Both analysts' views agree in direction; the numbers below come from the rows unless flagged. Rows per year in the file are 62 (2024), 86 (2025) and 47 (2026), plus 12 pre-2024.

Vision side. In 2024 two-hand work centred on single third-person RGB images evaluated on InterHand2.6M (HaMeR, BiTT, InterHandGen, AttentionHand), and datasets came from studio multi-view RGB plus optical markers (OakInk2, TACO). In 2025-2026 the input moved to egocentric or moving monocular video, with SLAM putting both hands in a world frame (HaWoR, Dyn-HaMR, EgoAllo, StableHand, the video-diffusion paper, MEgoVista). Consumer headsets became both the sensor and the label source: Aria and Quest 3 in HOT3D, Vision Pro in EgoDex, Aria in EgoMimic and EgoBridge. Analyst B's keyword count over the sensing field, which is approximate, puts the egocentric share at about 18 percent in 2024 and about 30 percent in 2025-2026, and the studio multi-view share falling from about 34 to about 13 percent. For scalable ground truth, dense markerless multi-view triangulation (GigaHands with 51 views, FurElise, AssemblyHands-X) is replacing markers. Capture rigs moved toward mobile and in-the-wild setups (SHOW3D, ACE-Data-0). Hand-object reconstruction moved to template-free Gaussian splatting from monocular RGB video (BIGS, GHOST).

Robotics side. Capture moved from puppet-arm teleoperation (Mobile ALOHA, 2024) to wearable or robot-free rigs: handheld SLAM grippers (UMI, HiFi-UMI, YUBI), exoskeletons (AirExo, AirExo-2, ACE), VR hand tracking (Open-TeleVision, Bunny-VisionPro) and phone or backpack interfaces (HoMMI, ModPack). It also moved to learning from internet or third-person monocular human video. Active head cameras appear in 2025-2026 (Active Vision, EgoMI, ActiveUMI). Non-visual channels (EMG, IMU, tactile, gaze, audio) appear almost only in 2025-2026 rows (EgoEMG, GazeHOI, TactiDex, ACE-Data-0, VTAO-BiManip), plus Signal2Hand in 2024.

Depth. A keyword match on RGB-D, depth, point cloud or Kinect in the sensing field hits 31 rows: 11 in 2024, 9 in 2025, 8 in 2026 and 3 pre-2024. The analysts reported about 27 and 34; the difference is keyword scope. These rows sit in handover (7), robot policies (6), fixed-rig datasets (4: HO-Cap, OphNet-3D, HOH, ADL4D), wearable datasets (3), capture rigs (3), human-video-to-robot (3: Bi-KVIL, DemoBot, ScrewMimic) and action recognition (2). No two-hand or two-hand-plus-object estimation method in the vision themes takes depth as input.
dataset_ecosystem:
Counts are string matches on the datasets field across all 207 rows, and both analysts got the same figures.

Evaluation hubs. ARCTIC is the hub of bimanual hand-object evaluation, named in 14 rows. It hosts the HANDS 2023, 2024 and 2025 tracks and is the main human source for physics retargeting (ManipTrans, object-centric dexterous manipulation, DexMachina). InterHand2.6M (11 rows) remains the only standard for two interacting hands without objects. After them come OakInk/OakInk2 and H2O (6 each), DexYCB, HOT3D, AssemblyHands and Bi-DexHands (4 each), then TACO, GRAB, FreiHAND, UmeTrack and KIT Bimanual Actions (about 3 each). GigaHands appears twice, as a dataset and as a retargeting source.

A weakness both analysts flag: per the rows, the HANDS ARCTIC category-agnostic track tests on a small pool of rigid-object clips, so several reconstruction claims rest on very little test data.

New 2024-2026 datasets in the rows:
- Human capture: OakInk2, TACO, BOTH57M, ADL4D, Ego-Exo4D, GigaHands, HOT3D, ParaHome, CORE4D, HUMOTO, HO-Cap, OphNet-3D, IndEgo, AssemblyHands-X, SHOW3D, EgoDex, EgoEMG, GazeHOI, ACE-Data-0.
- Generation and performance corpora: HandX, 3D-HIW, FoundHand-10M, FurElise, PianoMotion10M, BANZ-FS.
- Robot-side corpora: AgiBot World, RDT's bimanual set, YUBI, HiFi-UMI-2K, RP1M.
- Handover sets: DexH2R, Hand2Bot, TransHand-14K.
- Simulated benchmarks: RoboTwin and RoboTwin 2.0, BiGym, TWIN, HumanoidGen, DexGarmentLab, TeleOpBench, TactiDex.

Ground truth comes from five sources:
- Optical marker mocap fused with multi-view RGB is still the accuracy reference (ARCTIC, OakInk2, TACO, HOT3D, HUMOTO).
- Markerless multi-view triangulation of learned 2D keypoints with MANO fitting is used for scale (GigaHands, FurElise, AssemblyHands, AssemblyHands-X). The labels inherit the 2D detector's biases. That the detector is often HaMeR-class is analyst knowledge, not row text.
- Multi-view RGB-D with semi-automatic fitting is used in HO-Cap, OphNet-3D, HOH and ADL4D.
- Consumer-device on-device tracking is accepted as ground truth in EgoDex (Vision Pro), and no independent accuracy check is reported in the row.
- Synthetic or relit rendering is used in RenderIH, Re:InterHand and TransHand-14K.

Robotics rows mostly evaluate by task success on their own tasks, with no shared dataset. Of the 101 robotics-theme rows, at least 25 say only own demonstrations or leave the dataset unchecked or unstated. Analyst A estimated that about 30 percent of 2025-2026 method rows name no evaluation dataset at the abstract level. I did not recount that figure.
saturated:
Single-image two-hand mesh recovery on InterHand2.6M (theme 1) is crowded and incremental. The 2025-2026 entries swap backbones or add priors on the studio benchmark: VM-BHINet's 2-3 percent MPJPE gain, DF-Mamba, A2J-Transformer-Plus and penetration-free diffusion add-ons. HaMeR and WiLoR are now the default front end that other themes consume.

Text- or trajectory-conditioned hand-object motion generation (theme 6, 17 rows) fills quickly with one recipe: a contact map or keystates, then diffusion or tokens, then optional physics. Entries include Text2HOI, DiffH2O, LatentHOI, BimArt, ManiDext, HOIGPT, StructBiHOI, Dex2HOI and HandX. They are evaluated on the same few mocap sets (GRAB, ARCTIC, OakInk, H2O) with generative metrics rather than physical validity.

Bimanual robot policies and simulated benchmarks (29 rows) and teleoperation or capture rigs (23 rows) are numerous. Each brings its own glove, exoskeleton, gripper or VR app, plus a self-collected dataset, and evaluates on its own tasks, so results are hard to compare. RoboTwin, RoboTwin 2.0, BiGym, TWIN and Bi-DexHands overlap.

Handover (21 rows) is a long-running ICRA/IROS topic with many small contributions and few shared benchmarks beyond HandoverSim and DexH2R.

Template-free Gaussian-splatting reconstruction of ARCTIC clips is narrow, challenge-driven and partly duplicated: BIGS at CVPR 2025 plus its HANDS 2024 report, GHOST at CVPR 2026 plus its HANDS 2025 report, and a second HANDS 2024 team report.
rare_or_absent:
Both analysts agree on the following gaps.

RGB-D input:
- Estimating two hands plus a manipulated object from commodity RGB-D, as a tracking method evaluated on a shared benchmark, is absent.
- Depth appears only in capture rigs (HO-Cap, OphNet-3D, ADL4D, HOH, CORE4D), robot-side handover and policy perception, and skeleton pipelines for action recognition. Every vision reconstruction method in the rows is RGB-only and gets metric scale from MANO priors or SLAM.

Online tracking:
- Real-time, causal tracking of both hands and an object is rare; only QORT-Former and WiLoR stress real time. The strongest reconstruction methods are offline per-sequence optimisation (BIGS, GHOST) or offline world-space pipelines.
- Long-duration tracking with drift reporting is nearly absent, as are failure-rate or latency budgets for online tracking and per-frame uncertainty. StableHand's quality weighting and UA-Fit's uncertainty weighting are the exceptions.
- No row evaluates downstream robot success as a function of hand-tracking error.

Ground truth and evaluation:
- Metric world-frame accuracy against an independent reference is rarely reported, especially for markerless or device-tracked labels (EgoDex, GigaHands, FurElise).
- Cross-dataset evaluation, ground-truth error analysis and physical plausibility of reconstructed contacts are uncommon.

Objects:
- Object-to-object and two-object bimanual handling appears only in generation (Dex2HOI).
- Deformable and articulated objects in perception rest mainly on ARCTIC. Articulation appears mostly in generation and robot transfer.
- Transparent objects appear only in handover rows.

Interaction settings:
- Passing an object between one's own two hands (self-handover) has one row, a taxonomy paper.
- Two-person collaborative capture is thin (CORE4D, HOH, IndEgo, MOCHI).

Other modalities and domains:
- Physical quantities such as force, mass and grasp stability appear only in MACS (mass conditioning) and in tactile robot rows.
- Non-visual sensing (EMG, IMU, tactile gloves) fused with cameras for hand pose appears in fewer than six rows.
- Surgical and industrial settings appear in one row each (OphNet-3D, IndEgo).

Reconciliation choices:
(1) Two-hand vision rows. The problem lens split these into no-object (20) and hand-plus-object (13). The method lens split them into feed-forward regression (21) and per-sequence optimisation (10). I kept the problem cut, because it separates the InterHand2.6M line from the ARCTIC hand-object line, and recorded the method mix inside each theme. Avatars and texture went to theme 1, Re:InterHand and RenderIH to the dataset theme.
(2) Egocentric and world-space. The analysts disagreed by more than 30 percent (13 vs 8), so I recounted. 14 rows fall in my theme: 6 world-space 4D, 2 forecasting, 4 headset multi-view or view-adaptation (UmeTrack, two MegoTrack reports, Single-to-Dual-View), and 2 others (EgoHandICL, the generative temporal pose-action transformer). The method lens's 8 equals the world-space plus forecasting core. The other 6 sit with the egocentric problem in my theme, not with the feed-forward image regressors.
(3) Learning from humans for robots. The problem lens had a single theme of 28; the method lens split it into human video to robot (19) and physics retargeting of mocap (12). I kept the method split, because perception from video and RL tracking of clean mocap are different research lines, and recounted 18 and 9. Guitar and MUSIC went to the performance theme, ArtiGrasp, HERMES and MOCHI to physics retargeting.
(4) Datasets. The problem lens had one dataset theme of 23; the method lens split studio (23) and egocentric/wearable (7). I kept the split because it carries the sensing shift, and recounted 19 fixed-rig and 8 wearable. BOTH2Hands and GazeHOI count as datasets, where analyst A had BOTH2Hands under generation. FurElise and PianoMotion10M went to performance.
(5) Performance. The problem lens kept music, fingerspelling and shadows as a theme of 8; the method lens scattered them. I kept the theme (8), because it is a coherent graphics and robotics line. BANZ-FS and Hand-Shadow Poser are in it, so "other" holds only the IJCV survey. FoundHand, AttentionHand and ManiVideo went to generation.
(6) Action understanding. The analysts had 8 and 12. My recount is 11: IROS constraint-learning rows, 2HandedAfforder and self-handover included; BANZ-FS excluded.

sensing_shift: Both analysts counted keyword hits on the sensing field. Both counts are approximate and they differ in absolute numbers (monocular RGB video 21/27/30 rows by the problem lens versus 31/37/38 by the method lens, over 149/157/109 rows for 2024/2025/2026), but they agree on direction. Monocular video rose to roughly a third of 2026 rows, while single-image input fell from about 15-16 percent to about 11 percent. The input of choice moved from a static crop to moving-camera video (phone, internet, egocentric), with camera motion estimated jointly with the body. Egocentric head-mounted sensing stayed high. Within it, 2024 rows mostly use body-facing fisheye or stereo rigs, often synthetic (UnrealEgo line), while 2025-2026 rows use real headset SLAM cameras and Aria-style outward-facing video plus device pose; hands are now estimated in world space from the same stream (HaWoR, StableHand, MEgoVista). Body-worn IMU rows peaked in 2025. Inertial work moved from 6-IMU accuracy toward 3-4 consumer devices with cheap add-on ranging or pressure (UWB, ToF, barometer, insoles). A separate wearable line of sEMG, FMG, EIT and gloves for hand and arm angles grew in robotics venues. Radar/RF appeared as a cluster in 2025 (about 10 rows, driven by NeurIPS and ICLR) and nearly vanished from partial 2026. LiDAR persisted at a steady level. Explicit single RGB-D or depth input is rare: about 8 method rows take it as primary body or hand input (RoHM optionally, ANIM, HandRT, SimpleDepthPose, BodyMAP overhead depth, Agent-to-Sim, OKAMI, contact-wrench estimation), plus 3-4 depth point-cloud hand rows. Multi-view RGB-D appears only as ground-truth or dataset infrastructure (InterCap, HuMMan, EPFL-Smart-Kitchen, I2M, EgoBody, mRI). Depth's former role of resolving monocular scale is now played by monocular depth estimators and feed-forward 3D foundation reconstructors (MASt3R/CUT3R-style) inside RGB-only pipelines (HAMSt3R, Human3R, UniSH, Hand3R, PhySIC), from 2025 onward. Calibrated multi-camera rigs appear mainly as ground-truth instruments, not as the input under study.
dataset_ecosystem: Dataset fields are abstract-level, and 'not stated / not named / not checked' appears in roughly 40-50 percent of rows (by my count over the merged themes, 199 of 439 rows), so named-dataset counts understate real use. Body evaluation converges on a few sets. 3DPW is named in about 19-20 rows. EMDB (EM-sensor ground truth with a moving hand-held camera) and RICH are the world-grounded benchmarks, with PROX for scene contact. Human3.6M and MPI-INF-3DHP are kept alive mainly by 2D-to-3D lifting rows. OCHuman, 3DPW-OC and CrowdPose serve occlusion. AMASS is the universal training source for motion priors and for synthesized IMU and VR-tracker signals. Synthetic rendering (BEDLAM, BEDLAM2.0 with moving cameras, GTA-Human, SynBody, UnrealEgo, EgoGen, EgoSim, VOccl3D) is now the main supervision for regressors. Hi4D, CHI3D and Harmony4D serve close interaction. Hands use FreiHAND, DexYCB, HO3D, InterHand2.6M, ARCTIC and AssemblyHands, with HOT3D and Ego-Exo4D emerging. Inertial work evaluates on DIP-IMU and TotalCapture; that this pair is the standard rests on knowledge, since most rows do not name it. In-bed work uses SLP, and EMG hands use emg2pose and EgoEMG. Ground truth falls into five types: (1) optical marker mocap (MOYO, AthletePose3D, RSP3D, emg2pose's 26-camera rig, IMU papers' references); (2) multi-view markerless SMPL fitting, a pseudo ground truth (Hi4D, CHI3D, RICH, Harmony4D, AssemblyHands-X, InterCap); (3) body-worn EM or inertial suits (EMDB, Nymeria, EgoBody3M; that Nymeria uses an Xsens suit rests on knowledge); (4) synthetic rendering with exact labels; (5) physical force sensors and simulation for dynamics (pressure mats and insoles, force plates in AddBiomechanics, simulated muscles in Muscles in Time and ImDy). 71 of 439 rows have type dataset and 7 more are benchmarks. The method lens gathered 56 of them into one dataset theme; this merge distributes them to the problem each one serves. They concentrate in non-RGB sensing (14), under-represented populations (10), egocentric (8) and physics (6), so cross-paper comparability outside RGB is weak. New in the window: Ego-Exo4D, Nymeria/NymeriaPlus, EgoBody3M, Harmony4D, BEDLAM2.0, emg2pose, EgoEMG, WorldPose, FreeMan, HardMo, VOccl3D, OcMotion, MotionPRO, MMVP, RELI11D, OctoNet, AddBiomechanics, Care-PD, InclusiveVidPose, EPFL-Smart-Kitchen, I2M. Only VOccl3D, OcMotion, 3DPW-OC and OCHuman target occlusion directly. VOccl3D is synthetic and OCHuman has only 2D labels, so real 3D ground truth under object-induced occlusion is scarce.
saturated: (1) Single-image camera-frame HMR is the most crowded formulation (56 rows). Many 2024-2025 rows change only the output parameterization (tokens, VQ latents, discrete diffusion, SO(3) flows, virtual markers) or the alignment trick (DPO, VLM preference alignment, test-time optimization), with small MPJPE deltas on the same 3DPW and Human3.6M numbers. Scaled foundation regressors (SMPLest-X, Sapiens/Sapiens2, SAM 3D Body) are absorbing it, and its 2026 count falls to 6. (2) 2D-to-3D skeleton lifting on Human3.6M (about 15 rows: Mamba, GCN positional encodings, discrete diffusion, multi-hypothesis or conformal scoring, loss-landscape ensembles) is incremental and largely disconnected from occlusion in real data. (3) Sparse-IMU 'X Inertial Poser' papers (16 titles follow the naming): each adds one sensor or one physics term on the same AMASS-synthesized training set and the same DIP-IMU and TotalCapture tests. (4) AR/VR three-point body estimation trained and tested on AMASS with synthetic trackers, with repeated architecture swaps (diffusion, codebooks, Fisher uncertainty) and rare real-device evaluation. (5) World-grounded monocular video HMR is converging on a WHAM/TRAM/GVHMR template. 2026 rows (OnlineHMR, HumanBA, DuoMo, Humans as Checkerboards) mostly re-split camera and human motion, make it online or multi-shot, or swap in a 3D foundation backbone, all evaluated on EMDB and RICH. (6) Egocentric fisheye pose keeps producing new synthetic datasets rather than a shared real benchmark. (7) Diffusion, score and flow matching is the default tool: the method lens counted 62 of 439 contribution sentences mentioning it.
rare_or_absent: (1) A single static RGB-D camera as the method input for body motion under occlusion is nearly absent. About 8 method rows use RGB-D or depth at all, and no body-capture method targets a fixed RGB-D sensor watching a person handle objects. RGB-D appears mostly as dataset infrastructure (InterCap, HuMMan, EPFL-Smart-Kitchen, I2M, EgoBody, mRI, MMVP). (2) Human-object manipulation is thin. Only 5 rows estimate object pose jointly with the human (I'M HOI, IMU-HOI, ECHO, EgoGrasp, InterCap). About 10 rows mention two hands or bimanual work, mostly egocentric hand-only or datasets (AssemblyHands-X, EgoEMG, DexRoam). None pairs whole-body arm tracking with object pose from one depth sensor. (3) Self-occlusion of the arms by the torso or by a held object, and occlusion by the manipulated object itself, are rarely isolated as the studied condition. Occlusion benchmarks mean synthetic occluders or other people (VOccl3D, 3DPW-OC, OCHuman). (4) Upper-body-only or seated tabletop capture with legs out of frame is effectively absent outside VR three-point tracking. (5) Fusion of a fixed depth camera with sparse IMUs is absent; Stereo-Inertial Poser and visual-inertial gloves are the closest. (6) Evaluation practice gaps: almost no row reports per-joint accuracy split by visibility or occlusion level against marker ground truth, metric (mm) world-frame error under a static camera, latency on commodity hardware, sensor synchronization, calibration error, or failure rates. Calibrated uncertainty (conformal, Fisher) appears in about 5 rows. (7) Registration between the human estimate and a robot or object frame is not studied. Robotics rows evaluate task success, so robot-view pose quality goes unmeasured except in HARPER. (8) Arm or joint-angle validation against clinical mocap is confined to a handful of arXiv, clinical or populations rows. (9) Long-duration capture and drift analysis, depth-sensor-specific issues (IR interference, flying pixels at limb boundaries, close-range depth holes), and game-engine or digital-twin replay of captured motion as an evaluation target do not appear.

sensing_shift: Both analysts agree, and the merged counts confirm, that 2024 was dominated by single-frame estimation from one static RGB or RGB-D image. The four single-frame method themes (instance-level, CAD-based unseen, model-free reference, category-level) hold 32 of 74 rows in 2024, 45 of 107 in 2025 and 18 of 74 in 2026. Without the model-free reference theme they hold 26, 35 and 9. Category-level has no 2026 row. Growth is in video. Online-model tracking plus the robustness layer goes 3 -> 11 -> 11 rows. Hand-object 4D reconstruction goes 6 -> 7 -> 11. Object-trajectory extraction for robot learning goes 4 -> 11 -> 6. Within tracking, a depth-free monocular RGB subgroup appears in 2025-2026 (MGS-Track, Prior-free Tracking, GRC-Pose, KV-Tracker, OnlineSplatter, RGBTrack, ProxyPose, SEI3D). It takes its geometry from foundation geometry or generative models (DUSt3R point maps, monocular depth, SAM3D, LRMs, multiview-diffusion image-to-3D) rather than a depth sensor. The same priors replace CAD models in model-free single-frame pose (HIPPo, InstantPose, One View Many Worlds, UnPose). Hand-object methods move toward monocular and egocentric RGB video, with world grounding from SLAM (WHOLE). Robotics rows go the opposite way and add sensors. Event cameras run 2 -> 2 -> 4 rows. Robot in-hand tactile and proprioceptive work runs 3 -> 9 -> 10, with tactile in 15 of those 22 rows. Body and object IMUs appear once (IMU-HOI 2026). Egocentric head-mounted capture (Aria, Quest, HoloLens) becomes the main new dataset setting: HOT3D, SHOW3D, EgoXtreme, BOP-H3, and egocentric trajectory mining. Calibrated multi-camera RGB-D appears almost only as a ground-truth capture device (HO-Cap, OphNet-3D, HOGraspNet, TACO, PACE). At inference, multi-view input appears only in AlignPose (multi-view RGB), MVTracker (multi-view RGB with depth, for points), the deformable Gaussian rows and one bin-picking row. No row tracks a hand-held rigid object with a multi-RGB-D rig at test time.
dataset_ecosystem:
Single-frame rigid pose is scored on the BOP core seven (LM-O, T-LESS, TUD-L, IC-BIN, ITODD, HB, YCB-V), named in 16 of 26 CAD-based unseen-object rows and 22 rows in total. Its ground truth is CAD alignment to static RGB-D captures, and occlusion there means object-object clutter. Category-level work uses NOCS REAL275 and CAMERA25. HouseCat6D and Omni6D/Omni6DPose (ROPE/SOPE) are emerging as harder replacements. Hand-held or gripper-held tracking runs on two small benchmarks, HO3D (8 rows) and YCBInEOAT (7 rows), with DexYCB (4), HOT3D (6), ARCTIC (4) and TACO (3) next; these counts are string matches over title and dataset fields. The following rests on both analysts' knowledge, not the rows: YCBInEOAT is a few robot-arm RGB-D videos, and HO3D ground truth is fitted by multi-camera optimisation rather than mocap. HOT3D is the main new hand-held source in the window. It has mocap ground truth and egocentric multi-view Aria/Quest video, and BOP 2024 adopted it as BOP-H3, which puts hand-held objects inside the standard pose benchmark for the first time. Bimanual or two-hand data come from ARCTIC and TACO (mocap), HO-Cap (multi-view RGB-D plus HoloLens, with handovers), OphNet-3D (surgery, multi-view RGB-D) and DexH2R (human-to-robot handover). Ground-truth sources across rows:
- optical mocap: HOT3D, ARCTIC, TACO, HOGraspNet object mocap
- multi-view RGB-D fitting: HO-Cap, HOGraspNet, OphNet-3D, HOI4D, PACE
- robot kinematics: PhoCaL
- pose-graph-refined pseudo-labels: DynOPETs
- 3D scanning: SHOWMe, MessyKitchens
- synthetic rendering: OmniPose6D, Event6D, RRTrack, GTR, TransHand-14K, PEGASUS
Several 2025-2026 occlusion and fast-motion tracking benchmarks are synthetic sets built by the authors of the tracker they evaluate (RRTrack, Built-In Recovery, GTR, Point2Pose). Robot in-hand tactile work has no shared benchmark: 14 of 22 rows name only their own experiments, and Feelsight is the single named set. Across all 269 rows, 122 have a dataset field that says not stated, not named, not checked, own data or none (keyword count). Per-theme dataset counts are therefore lower bounds. Analyst B gave about 60 for method rows only and analyst A about 131; both are consistent with this count under different keyword sets.
saturated: The most crowded area is single-image 6D pose on static benchmarks. It covers three themes: CAD-based unseen objects on BOP (26), instance-level occlusion, symmetry and uncertainty on LM-O/YCB-V/T-LESS (24), and category-level on REAL275 (20 method rows). Together that is 70 of 269 rows (26 percent), or 95 rows (35 percent) with the model-free reference theme. Papers mostly vary one component of a shared pipeline: the feature backbone (DINOv2 or Stable Diffusion features), the generative head (diffusion or flow matching over keypoints, NOCS or SE(3)), or the correspondence-pruning and refinement detail. The benchmarks stay the same. The analysts' own knowledge, not the rows, adds two points: REAL275 accuracy is near ceiling, and BOP core gains between 2024 and 2025 methods are a few AR points. Category-level has no 2026 row, which fits saturation, but ICCV's absence in even years is a confound. Six instance-level rows are TPAMI or IJCV journal versions of 2021-2023 conference work. Model-free reference-based pose (25) is turning incremental too: many 2025-2026 entries swap in the newest image-to-3D or reconstruction foundation model to build the proxy, inside near-identical one-reference RGB-D formulations. In the robot-learning-from-video theme (21), pose tracking is a commodity, and novelty sits in how the trajectory is used. The tracker robustness layer (11) is beginning to repeat FoundationPose-plus-recovery designs, each with its own self-built synthetic benchmark.
rare_or_absent:
These matter for tracking objects handled by two human hands, and the rows barely cover them.
(1) Multi-view calibrated RGB-D as the estimation input for tracking a hand-held rigid object. No method row fuses several depth cameras to track an object while hands occlude it. Multi-view RGB-D appears only in ground-truth capture rigs (HO-Cap, OphNet-3D, HOGraspNet, PACE) and in point or deformable tracking (MVTracker).
(2) Bimanual handling as the estimation problem. Two-hand settings appear almost only in datasets (TACO, ARCTIC, HO-Cap handovers, OphNet-3D, DexH2R) and robot-learning pipelines (DexMan, Do as I Do). No pose or tracking method is evaluated on hand-to-hand transfer or the occlusion switching it causes. HANDS23 names close two-hand-object contact as an unsolved failure mode.
(3) The human hand pose used as a constraint or cue for object tracking. Only ComPose, the interaction-timeline grasp constraints, HOIC/HandyPriors physics and the handover depth restoration do this. By contrast, 22 rows use robot-hand touch or proprioception.
(4) Human-side wearable sensing. Only ViTaM-D (tactile glove) and IMU-HOI (body IMUs plus an object IMU).
(5) Standard evaluation of tracking under occlusion. YCBInEOAT and HO3D clips are short. Occlusion-aware metrics appear only in WALDO and TAPVid-3D. New occlusion and fast-motion benchmarks are mostly self-built and synthetic.
(6) Long-horizon metric accuracy (mm and deg over time, drift, recovery latency, failure-recovery rates) on long real sequences. Throughput claims exist (Event6D, KV-Tracker, SEI3D CPU-only) but there is no common protocol.
(7) Fiducial or mocap ground truth for validating learned trackers. Six marker rows exist, but none compares against learned trackers, and no learned-tracker row uses marker ground truth apart from the mocap datasets.
(8) Calibration error, cross-camera time synchronisation and consumer depth noise as evaluation variables. DTTDNet (iPhone LiDAR depth noise) is the only depth-noise row, and none treats calibration or synchronisation.
(9) Deformable or articulated hand-held objects under human-hand occlusion: only ArtHOI and ViTaM-D.
(10) Transparent or reflective hand-held objects: only the handover depth restoration, SilRef (robot) and stereo handover.
(11) Long out-of-view periods in egocentric video: only Where and What, Lost & Found and WHOLE.
(12) Uncertainty carried through time. The six uncertainty rows are single-frame; only UA-Pose, UniTac2Pose and Temporally Consistent Object 6D Pose propagate it.

Where the cuts differ and how each was resolved:
(a) Datasets. A split dataset rows into hand-object datasets (14) and rigid benchmarks (16). It spread 13 more dataset rows into problem themes: category-level datasets to category-level, OnePose/Gen6D to model-free, tracking datasets to tracking, YCB-Ev to event. B used one 43-row bucket. The disagreement exceeded 30 percent, so I re-read all 43 rows. I kept A's two-way split because hand-object capture and rigid-object benchmarking are distinct communities with different ground-truth methods. I kept B's choice of grouping all rigid data rows together, giving 29, so that method themes count methods only. This is why category-level is 20 and not A's 25, and model-free is 25 and not 28. TAPVid-3D moved to dense point tracking and PEGASUS to rigid datasets.
(b) Tracking. A had one 29-row theme. B split it into an online-model tracker theme (14) and a robustness and filter theme (15), with the persistence rows inside the filter theme. I kept B's split because it separates the reconstruction-while-tracking line from the systems layer. I moved five rows from B's filter theme into A's persistence theme: Object Permanence Filter, Out of Sight Still in Mind, KARL, Where and What, and Lost & Found. I added the light-field tracker to the robustness theme, which gives 11.
(c) Physics. B's physics theme (10) mixed robot contact tracking, hand-object physics, multi-object scene consistency and deformable Gaussians. A's cut separates these research lines better. TwinTrack and Vysics went to robot in-hand. HOIC and HandyPriors went to hand-object. Nonprehensile multi-object tracking, Picasso, simulation-ready scene estimation and MessyKitchens went to persistence (9). Both Gaussian-particle rows went to dense and deformable tracking (6).
(d) Smaller moves:
- S2P3 (polarization) went to instance-level, not event; A's choice, since its problem is self-supervised single-image pose.
- ArtReg went to articulated (A).
- Robot See Robot Do went to robot learning (A's cut).
- ViserDex and Omni-Scan went to robot in-hand (22, matching A).
- The reactive human-to-robot handover system (T-RO 2025) went to hand-object perception. A had it in other and B in robot learning; it perceives a human hand and held object rather than mining trajectories.
- The marker theme drops the invisible-marker deformable tracker (moved to dense, as A did) and keeps 6 rows.
(e) Remaining A-versus-B differences are under 30 percent and come from the moves above: instance 24 vs 23, hand-object 24 vs 23/21, event 8 vs 9/10.

- Single-frame share. A gave 29/35/9 single-frame rows for 2024/2025/2026 because it included category-level dataset rows. The merged method-only figures are 26/35/9, or 32/45/18 with model-free reference.
- Rows with no dataset named. A said about 131 and B about 60 (method rows only). My keyword count over all rows is 122; the gap comes from keyword sets and scope, not from a contradiction in the data.

themes.name: Egocentric human manipulation data as action-labelled training data: corpora plus co-training or VLA pretraining with retargeted wrist/hand actions
themes.what_papers_do: Treat the human as another embodiment: 3D wrist and finger trajectories from Project Aria or Vision Pro device tracking, or MANO pseudo-labels from monocular hand reconstruction on egocentric video, become actions in a shared or retargeted action space, and a policy or VLA is co-trained on human plus a small amount of robot data, sometimes with latent-space alignment (optimal transport, interpolation, high-noise-only diffusion). Method mix: about half co-training recipes (EgoMimic, EgoBridge, ImMimic, X-Diffusion, H-RDT, EgoZero), about half 2026 corpus or capture-pipeline releases of hundreds to tens of thousands of hours (EgoVerse, OpenEgo, Open-AoE, HumanNet, EgoScale, MINT, SABER, Ego-OSCAR).

themes.name: Imitating a specific task from one or a few human videos (explicit motion intermediates, video-conditioned skill policies, or VLM/symbolic task structure)
themes.what_papers_do: Given one or a few RGB or RGB-D videos of a person doing a task, recover something embodiment-agnostic and convert it to robot actions for the same task in a new scene. Method mix (approximate, from merged assignment): about 30 rows extract a per-video geometric intermediate (object 6D/SE(3) trajectories, bimanual hand keyposes, screw axes, object graphs, functional tool frames, keypoints; DITTO, ORION, OKAMI, YOTO, MimicFunc, RSRD); about 10 train a track, flow or 3D-motion predictor on video corpora that conditions the policy (Track2Act, ATM, Im2Flow2Act, General Flow, VidBot); about 8 learn video-prompted or cross-embodiment skill-embedding policies (Vid2Robot, UniSkill, MimicDroid, mismatched execution); about 10 parse the demonstration into plans, behaviour trees or constraint graphs with VLMs/LLMs, sometimes with force/EMG/audio; 2 use per-task real-to-sim (TieBot, Tool-as-Interface).
themes.trend: falling in share (about 20 percent of 2024 rows to 7 percent of 2026 rows) as bulk co-training and data engines take over

themes.name: Hand-object perception from casual video for robots: world-space 4D hand and hand-object reconstruction, articulation estimation, and video-to-dexterous-robot data engines

themes.name: Physics-simulation RL that turns human hand-object references into executable dexterous robot-hand motion (neural trackers, residual correction, curricula, physics-in-the-loop retargeting)
themes.what_papers_do: Take kinematic hand-object sequences from mocap datasets (ARCTIC, OakInk2, TACO, GigaHands) or reconstructed from video, and learn in Isaac Gym-type simulation a controller or a physically feasible trajectory that reproduces the object motion with a robot hand: residual modules over retargeting (ManipTrans), data flywheels (DexTrack), decaying virtual object controllers (DexMachina), quasi-physical simulator curricula, reference-scoped exploration, physics-in-the-loop optimisation (SPIDER, Grasp-and-Lift), then occasionally sim-to-real distillation. Method mix: about 14 rows consume mocap references, about 5 consume video-derived references (ViViDex, DexMan, PianoMime); the object trajectory is the target and the human hand a soft reference.

themes.what_papers_do: Estimate the human hand/arm per frame, inpaint it out and render or generate a robot arm, gripper or dexterous hand performing the corresponding motion (or translate the whole clip with a generative model), so that human video becomes robot-looking observation-action pairs for policy training or VLA pretraining; includes paired datasets and benchmarks for this editing.
