sensing_shift: Reconciled keyword tally over the sensing field of all 496 rows (2024: 110 rows, 2025: 206, 2026: 172; regex on free text, approximate). Egocentric or head-worn capture (egocentric, Aria, glasses, head-worn/head-mounted, Vision Pro) rises 11 -> 41 -> 53 rows, about 10 -> 20 -> 31 percent, driven by Project Aria Gen 1 then Gen 2, Vision Pro hand tracking and head-mounted smartphones; it feeds the new egocentric co-training/corpus theme (35 of its 41 rows) and the forecasting and pixel-translation themes. Handheld/UMI-style devices go 4 -> 8 -> 13 rows and gloves 2 -> 3 -> 10. Contact channels (tactile, force, torque, pressure, EMG, contact microphones) go 5 -> 24 -> 19 rows, but tactile alone only 3 -> 14 -> 14; almost all of them sit on worn or handheld devices, not on vision. VR/AR/XR headsets as teleoperation input peak in 2025 (7 -> 19 -> 8) as teleoperation shrinks in share. Mocap mentions go 14 -> 24 -> 12; optical mocap stays in vision datasets (ground truth) and humanoid retargeting (source motion) and does not migrate into robot-learning capture. Static third-person RGB-D (RGB-D/depth mentions 14 -> 24 -> 20) is the 2024 default for one-shot imitation (DITTO, ORION, OKAMI, MimicFunc) and is flat in count, falling in share. Monocular RGB is flat in count (21 -> 26 -> 30) but changes role from per-task trajectory extraction to bulk 4D hand-object reconstruction and pseudo-labelling with foundation-model stacks (HaWoR/WiLoR-type hands, metric depth, image-to-3D), and pixel-space editing or generation increasingly stands in for capture. Calibrated multi-camera rigs (multi-view mentions 5 -> 13 -> 9) are mostly vision capture studios. Net: from a robot in the loop and a fixed third-person camera toward cameras and sensors worn by the human, plus video-only pipelines. Confound (both analysts agree): arXiv rows go 3 -> 26 -> 51 and IROS/CoRL 2026 lists are thin, so 2026 shares overstate preprint-heavy lines.
dataset_ecosystem: No dominant shared benchmark: evaluation is mostly real-robot success on the authors' own tasks, not comparable across papers. Both analysts count about 98 rows introducing a dataset; the problem lens counts about 132 rows citing only own data and about 125 naming no dataset, the method lens counts only about 73 rows naming any recognisable public dataset (different regexes; the reading is the same). Most-cited external datasets: UMI-format data (about 12 rows), Ego4D (about 10), EPIC-KITCHENS (7), YCB/YCB-V (7), OakInk/OakInk2 (6), TACO (6), HOT3D (6), ARCTIC (5), DexYCB (5), EgoDex (5), CALVIN (5), H2O (5), Ego-Exo4D, Open X-Embodiment, HOI4D, Bi-DexHands (4 each), LIBERO (3). Ground truth splits in two. Perception datasets (ARCTIC, OakInk2, TACO, HOT3D, GigaHands, HO-Cap, DexYCB, HO3D, HOI4D) use optical marker mocap or dense multi-view fitting, are published mainly at CVPR/ICCV/ECCV, and are consumed mostly by the physics-tracking, reconstruction and forecasting themes and by the HANDS 2025/2026 dexterous tracking challenges. Robot-learning corpora of 2025-2026 (EgoDex 829 h, EgoVerse 1,362 h, OpenEgo 1,107 h, Open-AoE 2,000 h, WiYH 1,000+ h, MINT 1,021 h, EgoScale 20,854 h, HumanNet 1M h, FastUMI-100K, YUBI 8,434 h, HiFi-UMI-2K, DexCanvas, HuRo 630K episodes, RoboEdit 174K clips) rely on device tracking (Vision Pro, Aria SLAM and hand tracking, handheld VIO) or monocular pseudo-labels, and the rows report no validation of those action labels against mocap. Robot-side evaluation uses CALVIN, LIBERO, SIMPLER, Bi-DexHands, RoboTwin, PerAct2. Tactile/force datasets (H-Tac, HT-Bench, TactiDex, VTDexManip, EgoTactile, FEEL, Hoi!) are the newest niche. Benchmarks built for this subfield are few and recent: UMI-Bench 1.0, TeleOpBench, H2R-Bench, HandEdit, TactiDex, HT-Bench, Mimicking-Bench, DexH2R, plus the HANDS challenges; RoboTube (2022) is the only older human-video-to-robot benchmark in the rows.
saturated: (1) Teleoperation interfaces (71 rows): VR, glove, exoskeleton and leader-arm variants with a retargeting module, each validated on its own demonstrations by task success and small user studies; differentiation is mostly cost, feedback modality or target platform. (2) UMI derivatives within the handheld-device theme: FastUMI, FastUMI-100K, exUMI, TacUMI, UMI-FT, HiFi-UMI, ActiveUMI, UMI on Legs, UMI-On-Air, UMI-Underwater, iPhone-based HoMMI and Behavior Prompting, each adding one sensor or one embodiment. (3) Egocentric co-training recipes with retargeted wrist/hand actions (EgoMimic, EgoBridge, ImMimic, In-N-On, EgoVLA, H-RDT, Ego-Pi, EgoZero, EMMA, Traj2Action, X-Diffusion) differing mainly in alignment loss and data scale, plus 2026 arXiv corpus releases with overlapping sources and near-identical pseudo-labelling pipelines that report hours rather than label accuracy. (4) Latent-action and video-token pretraining (LAPA, UniVLA, Moto, CLAP, Joint-Aligned Latent Action, ViPRA, LDA-1B) on the same CALVIN/LIBERO/SIMPLER evaluations. (5) Humanoid motion retargeting and RL tracking (40 rows including humanoid teleop) converging on the same artefact list: foot sliding, penetration, contact preservation (GMR, OmniRetarget, I-CTRL, rig unification, ReActor). (6) Language-guided dexterous grasp generation on object point clouds at ICCV/NeurIPS.
rare_or_absent: Both lenses agree: quantitative validation of the captured human demonstration itself is nearly absent outside the vision datasets. Wrist and fingertip error, object 6-DoF pose error, contact timing and inter-camera or inter-device synchronisation against independent ground truth appear only in dataset papers and a few devices (FSGlove against optical mocap, FLiPo, HiFi-UMI); robot-learning papers treat HaMeR/FoundationPose/CoTracker-class or device-tracker outputs as truth. Calibrated fixed multi-camera RGB-D capture of bimanual object handling, with marker-based object poses, used directly as robot supervision is rare (OKAMI, YOTO with stereo, ORION with an iPad, DemoBot with single RGB-D are single-camera exceptions). Bimanual inter-hand coordination is mostly captured with two handheld grippers or exoskeletons rather than estimated from vision under hand-hand and hand-object occlusion; in-hand object pose under heavy occlusion during bimanual transfer is essentially absent. Deformable and articulated object state in demonstrations is rare (TieBot, cloth folding, RSRD, ArtiPoint, PokeNet, SSFold). Contact and force estimated from vision rather than worn sensors appears only in EgoTactile and reconstruction-based contact priors; measured ground-truth force only in ForceMimic, UMI-FT and Hoi!. Metric-scale verification of monocular reconstructions is absent. Also nearly absent: shared real-world human-to-robot benchmarks with fixed tasks and protocols; head-to-head comparisons of capture modalities on the same tasks (only How to Train Your Robots, Is a Simulation better than Teleoperation, TeleOpBench, the CVPR 2026 data utilization law); capture latency and synchronisation reporting; failure, uncertainty and recovery demonstrations (HRDexDB an exception); repeated-trial variance or significance; cross-lab reproducibility (EgoVerse multi-lab study an exception); privacy and consent handling for egocentric corpora; two-person collaborative capture beyond handover; event, thermal or radar sensing; and industrial, clinical and caregiving demonstrations beyond IndEgo, OpenRoboCare and the bathing-assistance capture paper.

sensing_shift: Based on the 239 rows dated 2024-2026 (15 rows are 2022-2023); 2026 is a partial year. (1) Representation shift, not a sensor shift: 3D Gaussians on a parametric mesh replaced NeRF and implicit surfaces in essentially all avatar, telepresence and volumetric-video rows by 2025 (the method analyst's keyword count, approximate: Gaussian or splatting rows 19 in 2024, 33 in 2025, 21 in partial 2026). (2) Capture moved down to commodity devices at use time while studio domes and light stages stayed the training-time sensor: feed-forward single-image or few-photo avatars (11 of 19 rows in 2025), phone-scan personalization of universal priors, single-webcam 3D video calls (VoluMe 2025, Mon3tr and Tele360 2026), and single-smartphone biomechanics and clinical measurement (OpenCap Monocular, Portable Biomechanics Laboratory, Quantitative Movement Testing, 2025-2026, mostly arXiv). Rows naming a phone, smartphone or webcam rose from about 5 in 2024 to about 12 in 2025 (keyword count, approximate). Deployment targets shifted to phones and standalone headsets (SqueezeMe, TaoAvatar, HRM^2Avatar, MUA, ESCA). (3) XR body tracking moved from three-point HMD plus controller signals and sparse IMUs (11 of 16 sparse-signal rows are 2024, 1 in 2026) to the headset's own body-facing cameras and Aria glasses (EgoBody3M 2024; FRAME, REWIND 2025; XR-Poser, EgoPoseFormer v2, visibility-aware estimation 2026). (4) Depth stays marginal: about 27 rows carry depth or LiDAR in their sensing field across all years, concentrated in robot-side teleoperation views (5 of 10), object digital twins (5 of 14), in-bed clinical sensing and older datasets (HuMMan, EgoBody, SLP, mRI, DNA-Rendering, SmartPortraits). Only DPHMs, ANIM, MorpheuS and the hand-face contact head avatar use consumer RGB-D as the main input for human reconstruction, and only OphNet-3D uses multi-view RGB-D for metric hand-object pose. (5) Clinical work moved from multi-camera lab setups (TULIP 6 cameras, AthletePose3D) toward validating single smartphone video against marker mocap. (6) Niche sensors appear once or twice each: event camera, EMG, force myography, UWB, barometers, mmWave.
dataset_ecosystem: Avatar work rests on studio capture and image metrics. Monocular fitting still uses the small, old ZJU-MoCap, PeopleSnapshot and NeuMan sets (NeRSemble for heads); feed-forward methods train and test on scan corpora (THuman2.0, X-Humans, HuGe100K). Large studio corpora supply priors and relighting ground truth: Ava-256, Goliath, Multiface, MVHumanNet and MVHumanNet++, DNA-Rendering, ActorsHQ, NeRSemble, RenderMe-360, HumanOLAT, many from one industrial lab or Shanghai AI Lab groups. Ground truth is held-out captured images scored with PSNR, SSIM and LPIPS (protocol stated from analyst knowledge, not rows), not geometry or pose. A large share of 2025-2026 avatar rows name no dataset and use in-house dome captures, so cross-paper comparison is weak. Sparse-signal XR tracking trains and tests on AMASS with synthesized tracker or IMU signals (MPJPE-style metrics, analyst knowledge), plus DIP-IMU, TotalCapture and UIP-DB. Egocentric body tracking gained large real datasets: EgoBody3M, Nymeria (ground truth from an inertial suit), NymeriaPlus, Ego-Exo4D, EgoBody, and UmeTrack plus HOT3D for hands. Clinical and inclusive work is mostly new small datasets every year (TULIP, Care-PD, ProGait, LDPose, InclusiveVidPose, RSP3D, A3D, REHAB24-6, AthletePose3D, SLP, mRI) with ground truth from clinician ratings (UPDRS) or marker mocap, and several private cohorts. Biomechanics leans on force-plate and EMG data (AddBiomechanics, MOYO, PianoKPM) and simulated muscle activations (Muscles in Time). Human-object rendering uses BEHAVE, HOSNeRF and NeuMan; OphNet-3D introduces metric hand-plus-instrument ground truth from multi-view RGB-D. Object digital twins have DTTD and DTTD-Mobile (RGB-D 6-DoF pose). Teleoperation retargeting and remote-scene interfaces have no shared benchmark: own scenes, tasks and user studies.
saturated: Monocular-video Gaussian avatar fitting (35 rows) is the most crowded and incremental line: papers differ in where the Gaussians are anchored (mesh, UV, surfels, blendshapes, local MLPs, Jacobians) and which diffusion prior fills unseen regions, with small PSNR or LPIPS gains on ZJU-MoCap or PeopleSnapshot. Single-image feed-forward Gaussian humans (19 rows, 11 in 2025, 7 at ICLR) are converging on one recipe: a large reconstruction transformer, optionally with multi-view diffusion, over SMPL-X. Studio codec avatars (21 rows) are a dense but narrow industrial line iterating on relighting, universal priors, distillation, quantization and headset driving. Three-point HMD to full body on synthetic AMASS signals peaked in 2024 (11 of 16 rows) with diffusion, stratified, uncertainty, codebook and IK variants on one protocol; its near-disappearance after 2025 suggests the benchmark is treated as solved and attention moved to headset cameras, not that real-world use is solved. Whole-body humanoid teleoperation from VR or RGB pose is a crowded systems area at CoRL, ICRA and IROS with similar retarget-plus-RL pipelines.
rare_or_absent: (1) Hands manipulating objects, especially with both hands: only 8 rows reconstruct a person or hands together with an object or scene, mostly as re-renderable Gaussians (6 of them 2025-2026, 3 on arXiv). Only OphNet-3D outputs metric bimanual hand and 6-DoF object poses. No avatar, telepresence or volumetric-video row tracks a held object in metric 3D for live use; ToMiE, DualGS and TaoGS handle held items only as appearance or topology. (2) Consumer RGB-D as the driving sensor for human tracking, avatars or clinical analysis is nearly absent (DPHMs, ANIM, MorpheuS, the hand-face contact avatar, in-bed depth); depth lives on the robot side of teleoperation, in object digital twins and in older datasets. (3) Metric accuracy: avatar and telepresence rows report image-similarity metrics; geometric, scale or pose error against an independent reference is seldom reported (metric norm partly analyst knowledge). (4) Clinical validation against marker mocap with patient cohorts is rare at top venues: the ARAT, reachable-workspace, Quantitative Movement Testing, OpenCap Monocular and HMR-validation rows are arXiv; only TULIP, Care-PD, ProGait, InclusiveVidPose and a few others sit at top venues. (5) Upper-limb clinical tasks with real object handling (ARAT-style grasp and move, pouring with orthosis) appear in only a handful of arXiv and ICRA rows; hand-function scoring from video during real object use is largely missing. (6) End-to-end motion-to-photon latency, network conditions and real-device deployment are measured only in codec-avatar and teleoperation rows; most real-time claims are desktop render FPS. (7) Multi-person telepresence with contact (GeoAvatar, MultiPly, multi-human rendering are offline), robustness to clinic or home lighting, clutter and camera placement (one physiotherapy row), long-duration monitoring, calibration and failure-mode reporting are rare. (8) Uncertainty estimates appear in 3 to 4 rows (FisherPoser, EnvPoser, biomechanics confidence intervals); privacy in one row (Care-PD anonymization); fairness across body types only in the 5 limb-deficiency and prosthesis rows.
